A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEPAL/BLOCS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–G support reliable comparison. Existing material can be matched across pagination and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original downstream prediction, link-prediction, scalability, ablation, and continual-learning results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations, including downstream prediction results in Figures 2–3 and supplementary experiments in Appendices C, E, F, and G.

M1.justification: Core selection, BLOCS Algorithm 1, core embedding training, propagation Equations 4–6, and the continual-learning adaptation remain unchanged. Revised explanations and new diagrams do not introduce different procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain seven large knowledge graphs and 46 downstream tables, alongside Mini YAGO3, the FB15k-237/YAGO3-10/Wikidata5M benchmark, link prediction, and the YAGO3 continual-learning scenario. The new evaluation diagram illustrates existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments, including the main baselines, SMORE and GraSH in Table 7, DistMult-ERAvg in Table 12, and partitioning comparisons. TIGER is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 corrects reported computational allocations from CPU nodes to cores, including 20 for PBG/DGL-KE and 88 for the clustering benchmark. This revises stated settings without establishing reruns; splits, preprocessing, metrics, model dimensions, and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The BLOCS removal and METIS replacement ablations, hyperparameter sensitivities, core-selection comparisons, performance correlations, communication analysis, and continual-learning experiment are retained. The new diagrams provide explanations rather than additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repeats of five-fold cross-validation, Friedman/Conover testing at alpha = 0.05, and 95% confidence intervals in the downstream-versus-link-prediction plots. No repeated-run counts or uncertainty-reporting procedures change.

E6.justification: All 15 tables and the 23 existing figures retain their results. For example, Table 15 still reports average performance of 0.962 for SEPAL-CL and 0.988 for SEPAL trained from scratch on YAGO3-2022. The two added diagrams contain no new experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1, its assumptions, the queriability definition, and Appendix D's derivations and proof are retained. Equation renumbering and moving the querying function inline do not change the mathematics; the added spectral discussion is an interpretive analogy.

C1.justification: The central claims about scalable embedding, BLOCS, positive-triple alignment, and downstream utility remain. Adding 'among positive triples' clarifies scope already explicit in v2's second contribution and Proposition 4.1. Continual-learning capability was already demonstrated in Appendix G.3.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds a graph-Fourier/low-frequency interpretation of propagation and explicitly connects queriability to maximizing positive-triple scores. It also explains how reducing negative-triple scores may compete with that objective. Existing applicability limits and bias discussion remain.

D1.justification: The code address changes from the personal repository to soda-inria/sepal, and the checklist replaces its future-release statement with a statement that code has been released. Appendix B.3 corrects hardware units from nodes to cores. Implementation and hyperparameter documentation otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds TIGER (Wang et al., 2024) and its slice-and-cache approach to large-scale inductive GNN training. Existing research positioning is retained; the RelBench publication-year correction concerns bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Limited paragraph rewrites clarify boundary-conditioned propagation and queriability, and the local-subsampling discussion is rearranged. Copyediting and author-contact changes also occur. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 5 illustrating downstream evaluation and Figure 13 illustrating BLOCS operations. Existing figures and tables are retained but redistributed, with corresponding renumbering and page reflow. The querying function formerly displayed as Equation 9 becomes inline.

improvement.justification: The new evaluation and BLOCS diagrams make existing procedures easier to understand, while corrected CPU units and updated code-access statements improve reproducibility reporting. These are useful, limited refinements: the experimental evidence, algorithm, and formal proofs remain unchanged, and no major scientific deficiency is resolved.
